description: Synthetic spend requests for the Challenge 2 UI workbench. Each scenario wraps one contract-shaped SpendRequest and labels the state it proves.
authorityWarning: Synthetic demo data only. This file is never an authority for roles or status. At integration and in the recorded demo, status and decisions must come from the server response.
identityNote: Display names are presentation only; they are never authorization input. The sub values below are stand-ins for the real TideCloak sub claims and must be reconciled with Person 2's realm before any end-to-end test.

scenarios.expectedExplanation: Pending. No reviewer has voted yet. Senior reviewer A, senior reviewer B and the CEO reviewer all still need to respond.
scenarios.proves: A new request starts Pending with all three reviewer slots waiting.

request.title: Accessible keyboard for the design workstation
request.businessReason: The current keyboard is not usable with the accessibility switch the new starter uses.

scenarios.expectedExplanation: Pending. Senior reviewer A approved. Senior reviewer B and the CEO reviewer have not voted. All three distinct approvals are required.
scenarios.proves: One approval is not enough, and each outstanding slot is named.

request.title: Team lunch after the Q4 release
request.businessReason: Twelve staff worked the release weekend; this covers a casual team lunch.

scenarios.stateLabel: Pending - 2 of 3 approved (both seniors, CEO waiting)
scenarios.expectedExplanation: Pending. Both senior reviewers approved, but the CEO reviewer has not voted. All three distinct approvals are required.
scenarios.proves: Two senior approvals still do not approve a request; the CEO is a separate required slot.

request.title: Annual licence for the design system tool
request.businessReason: The client rebrand needs shared component libraries; the licence is annual and per-seat.

scenarios.stateLabel: Denied - senior reviewer B rejected (no prior approvals)
scenarios.expectedExplanation: Denied. Senior reviewer B rejected this request. One rejection is final; later approvals cannot reverse it.
scenarios.proves: A single rejection at a senior slot denies immediately.

request.title: Standing desk for the support bay
request.businessReason: Two support staff share the bay and requested height-adjustable desks.

decisions.comment: Existing desks meet the ergonomic standard.

scenarios.stateLabel: Denied - CEO rejected after both seniors approved
scenarios.expectedExplanation: Denied. The CEO reviewer rejected this request after both senior reviewers approved. One rejection is final; later approvals cannot reverse it.
scenarios.proves: Rejection by the CEO is equally final, even when two approvals already exist.

request.title: Conference travel to the Singapore service design summit
request.businessReason: Three workshops are directly relevant to the current client project.

scenarios.stateLabel: Approved - all three distinct reviewers approved
scenarios.expectedExplanation: Approved. Senior reviewer A, senior reviewer B and the CEO reviewer all approved this request.
scenarios.proves: Only all three distinct approvals produce Approved.

request.title: Accessibility audit of the checkout flow
request.businessReason: An external audit is required for the Q4 accessibility milestone.

decisions.comment: Budget is available in the current quarter.
Approved - required for the Q4 accessibility milestone.

scenarios.stateLabel: Denied - terminal rejection with later approvals recorded (display robustness)
scenarios.expectedExplanation: Denied. Senior reviewer A rejected this request, and that decision is final. Later approvals from senior reviewer B and the CEO reviewer cannot reverse it.
scenarios.proves: The explanation logic must treat a rejection as terminal even if later approval records are present.
scenarios.note: SYNTHETIC DISPLAY FIXTURE: a correct server refuses votes after denial with 409 and would never persist this shape. It exists only so the UI can be checked against a hostile or inconsistent record; the UI must still read Denied.

request.title: Incentive payments for the customer research panel
request.businessReason: Twenty panel participants need a small voucher for a ninety-minute session.

decisions.comment: This duplicates the study already funded in September.
I support the panel; the September study covered a different segment.

scenarios.stateLabel: Pending - 2 of 3 approved (senior A and CEO, senior B waiting)
scenarios.expectedExplanation: Pending. Senior reviewer A and the CEO reviewer approved, but senior reviewer B has not voted. All three distinct approvals are required.
scenarios.proves: The CEO approval does not stand in for a senior reviewer; the missing senior slot is named.

request.title: Replacement on-call phone
request.businessReason: The current handset no longer holds a charge through an on-call shift.

decisions.comment: Replacement is cheaper than a failed on-call response.
